conventions.convention: Proper means continuous with compact inverse images of compact subsets; subset compactness uses the subspace topology. The analytic operations use locally compact Hausdorff spaces.
The functor f_! uses sections whose closed support maps properly to the base. Its finite resolution terms need only be c-soft on each fibre.

The initial exceptional Hom transposition has bounded source objects and bounded-below target objects, under a uniform compact-support dimension bound for every sheaf on every open of every fibre. A full bounded constructible adjunction follows after geometric preservation is proved.
Positive complex orientation gives ω_X = k_X[2d] on a smooth complex d-fold; duality is R internal Hom into ω_X.
The ordinary middle-perverse upper bound on a stratum S is H^q(i_S^*A) = 0 for q > −dim_C S; the lower bound is H^q(i_S^!A) = 0 for q < −dim_C S. The IC heart input is L[dim_C Z].
AC is assumed, coefficients may be any field, and the category is ordinary bounded algebraically constructible analytic sheaves on separated finite-type complex varieties.
For a smooth map of pure relative complex dimension d, perverse normalization is a^*[d], while extraordinary pullback is a^*[2d]. Reflection and conservativity require surjectivity.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and let k be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to D_c^b with the three adjunctions, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula and trace. Proper f has Rf_! = Rf_*. Verdier duality is involutive and exchanges the adjoints; smooth complex orientation gives ω_X = k_X[2d], and smooth relative dimension d gives f^! = f^*[2d]. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs.

Under AC, over any field, the stated stratum support and cosupport inequalities define a bounded middle-perverse t-structure on D_c^b of a separated finite-type complex variety, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Duality exchanges the aisles. Its heart is abelian of finite length, with simple objects the intersection complexes of simple finite-rank local systems on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports. Open restriction is perverse exact, heart objects have no negative Hom, and simple endomorphism rings are division k-algebras.

Under AC and the uniform all-fibre-open dimension bound d, for a continuous map of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, f_! is left exact, (Rf_!A)_y is fibrewise compact-support cohomology, and Rf_! maps bounded derived categories into bounded derived categories. The exceptional candidate represents Hom(Rf_!A,B) = Hom(A,f^!B) for bounded A and bounded-below B, with lower bound inf(B) − d. After geometric bounded constructibility is established, this is a right adjunction on the bounded constructible subcategory.

Under AC and the stated actual finite conical, triangulation and incidence suppliers, ω_X and D_X preserve bounded constructible objects on separated finite-type complex varieties, and natural bidual evaluation is an isomorphism. Smooth complex orientation gives ω_X = k_X[2d]. For constructible maps with the geometrically proved bounded outputs, duality exchanges Rf_* and Rf_!, computes f^! = D_Xf^*D_Y, and gives coherent extraordinary proper base change.

Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, proper-support Cartesian base change, proper equality, bounded-factor projection formula and canonical direct-image composition hold. Exceptional composition and trace coherence hold on the subsequently proved bounded constructible specialization. Closed inclusions have the derived closed-support description and both localization triangles; locally, R internal Hom(i_*k_Z,A) = RΓ_ZA. Extraordinary dual base change is not claimed before constructible biduality.

Under AC and the actual geometric and incidence suppliers, the six operations on the proved analytic algebraic constructible subcategory have their adjunctions and coherent composition, proper base change, projection, localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. Product projections have the stated finite cochain comparison and ordinary unit. Smooth base change for Rf_* is asserted for the supplied open-proper factorization with the stated conical models, and for proper maps. Finite constructible models commute with coefficient extension.

Closed inclusions and composites are proper; properness is preserved by base change when the original target is Hausdorff; fibres are compact; closed-source restrictions are proper; and a proper map into a locally compact Hausdorff target is closed. No choice principle is used.

concerns.concern: Fact F8 says that 'properness of the support map into a locally compact Hausdorff space forces that support to be closed in the base'. The support is a subset of the source, so this is incorrectly typed. The cited stability lemma gives closedness of its image in the base, which is the conclusion actually used in step 1.2. The theorem's argument needs only that corrected wording.

seams_checked.note: Constructibility, finite-rank local systems, bounded derived conventions and constant-polyhedral comparison retain their stated hypotheses.

The resolution hypothesis is uniform over all sheaves and all opens of all fibres. Fibrewise softness is distinguished from global softness; the field-linear generator construction is supplied locally.
Quasi-projective geometric constructions are used on affine pieces, with finite affine-open descent for general separated finite-type varieties. No global simplicial presentation of a map is assumed.
Finite deleted-boundary incidence models and local product comparisons are used within their scope. Internal Hom is not replaced by Hom of stalks, and coefficient extension uses finite models.
The family and fixed-part items use proper fibre comparison, derived direct-image composition and local product cohomology for smooth projective families; semisimplicity is supplied separately.
Support bounds, duality, localization, finite-length hearts and adjunctions agree with the ordinary suppliers. Affine vanishing and noncharacteristic pullback are separately proved.
Recollement, boundary subobject/quotient characterizations, proper duality and coefficient extension are faithful. Hard Lefschetz, splitting and semisimplicity are additional downstream arguments.

Ordinary operations are transported through finite resolutions. Smooth perverse pullback uses [d], extraordinary pullback uses [2d], and surjectivity supplies reflection. Equivariant normalization is established downstream.
Proper extraordinary exchange, dualizing transitivity, trace coherence and positive complex orientation are cited faithfully. Singular supports are not assigned a smooth-manifold dualizing shift.
Proper base change and its face/degeneracy naturality are used with bounded constructible coefficients and a common lower bound. Fibre acyclicity is not inferred from the supplier.
